newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - India drifts off as Bombay ends mixed.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - India drifts off as Bombay ends mixed.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts ended mixed on Tuesday, following local market uncertainty earlier and as prices continued their drift off recent highs, dealers said.
They said the market remained set for further strength but was consolidating.
He said Reliance had picked up after losses on Monday but other key stocks had slipped, to leave the GDR market slightly softer overall.
Reliance added 60 cents to $22.15/$23.15, while Hindalco lost 40 cents to $35.35/$36.35. VSNL lost 62 cents to $18.80/$19.10.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index closed 0.65 points lower at 87.17, down 0.74 percent, with the premium over the local market at 19.00 percent from 20.85 percent.
Bombay's benchmark index added 14.94 points to 4,306.39.
The HSBC James Capel Korea GDR Index softened again as the market continued to consolidate in Seoul following a recent strong run.
The index shed 1.12 points to 77.22 points, a premium of 41.60 percent over the local market.

The Capel Taiwan GDR Index finished 0.04 points higher at 129.22, representing a discount to the local market of 2.66 percent. The local market's weighted index eased on Tuesday, after a touching a seven year high in intra-day trade on Monday.
